text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali says that Jordan is against terrorism; stresses kingdom's belief in dialogue as a means to build confidence.
- 1.5 million voters expected to be included on the electoral lists of the coming parliamentary elections due next November, says interior minister.
- Deputy Prime Minister Abdullah Ensour says the government is ready to open a dialogue with the Islamists who took a decision to boycott the coming elections.
- King Hussein and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat discuss the difficult situation in the occupied territories.
- Cabinet discusses on Tuesday setting date for parliamentary elections.
- An international and regional appeal to King Hussein to intervene with an initiative to save the Middle East peace process.
- King Hussein and Arafat discuss the crisis in the Palestinian track.
- Jordanian deputies boycott meeting with a delegation of visiting Israeli lawmakers.
